title: Cost: GPU, mixed precision, and training time against the gain

videos.script: A network is described by its parameters. The bill is decided by something else. {{bill}} This lesson counts what training costs, in operations, in bytes and in hours. {{count}} Lesson 9's network does two operations per parameter, for every example. Lesson 11's convolutional network does almost eighteen, because each filter slides over the whole image. {{reuse}} A training step costs about three forward passes. That gives the rule used to budget large models: six, times the parameters, times the examples. {{rule}} Then memory. Weights, gradients and Adam's two buffers come to sixteen bytes per parameter. The activations grow with the batch. {{memory}} Sixteen-bit numbers save some of that. Trained in bfloat16, the convolutional network reaches the same accuracy. {{bf16}} Put one autocast in the wrong place, though, and the network learns nothing at all. {{trap}} When a batch does not fit, four small ones can add up to the same gradient. {{accumulate}} Then a price per hour turns the time into a bill. The price in this lesson is a variable, not a quote. {{price}} Last, what the money buys. Each doubling of the epochs buys less than the one before. {{returns}} More images were still paying when the digits ran out. {{end}}
